findings: README Configuration documents precedence across global, trusted-project, and runtime settings; runtime settings clear on session lifecycle events and untrusted project configuration is ignored.

config.test.ts distinguishes invalid-value behavior: rewindHintReserveTokens blocks fallback, whereas anchorStartAfterTurns and parentHandoffMode fall through. These are documented/test-specified behaviors, not executed tests.
Likely disclosure concern: proposal-engine.test.ts indicates calls-only includes tool arguments while omitting results/details; users may not infer that arguments are still disclosed.
auto-navigate-config.ts strictly parses settings, bounds integer cadence/token values, and merges tool policies field-wise.

proposal-command.ts modelProposal confirms full textual history across branches is sent to the model; tool disclosure rules and binary omission are surfaced. Likely concern: confirmation does not explain calls-only payload sanitization.
The full-history remote disclosure is verified from source; no tests are claimed as run.
README.md says retrospective proposals send full textual history by default and tool exclusions do not redact copies embedded in prose or summaries, a likely disclosure hazard given the default.
auto-navigate.ts builds a bounded structured payload using configured tool rules and explicitly omits older evidence when constrained; config.ts layers global, trusted-project, and runtime settings.

continuity-capture.ts supplies a capped user message and prioritized active items to a classifier, while captured text remains verbatim; continuity-briefing.ts prioritizes objectives/goals/rules/decisions over facts, file pointers, and steering under budget pressure.
extensions/navigate-tree/config.ts merges configuration layers; invalid proposal settings block model proposals, while invalid hint settings disable the hint rather than falling back.
extensions/navigate-tree/proposal-options.ts defines per-tool disclosure modes full, calls-only, and omit; configuration validation rejects invalid disclosure rules.

Classifier workflows can receive user text: partition 3's continuity-capture.ts constructs bounded classifier context and retains captured text verbatim, a disclosure consideration rather than a confirmed defect.
